relationships.subject: resiniferatoxin
relationships.evidence_quote: the ablation of TRPV1-positive nerve endings mediated by intrathecal [138,145] or epidural [149] RTX results in lasting pain relief

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: Cancer pain is reduced in TRPV1-null mice compared to in wild-types [76,92].

relationships.subject: IGF-1
relationships.evidence_quote: In a rat model of bone cancer pain, IGF1 was found to up-regulate TRPV1 expression in sensory afferents [72].

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: TRPV1-expressing nerve endings release calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) that, in turn, can stimulate cancer growth [73,74,75].

relationships.subject: bradykinin
relationships.evidence_quote: TRPV1 is activated by changes in pH (in particular, by protons) [31,32] and represents a downstream target for various pain-generating substances, as exemplified by bradykinin [33,34].

key_findings: Review: TRPV1+ afferent ablation (intrathecal/epidural RTX) or high-dose capsaicin patches relieve cancer/CIPN pain, but effects of TRPV1 blockade on cancer progression are conflicting across models.
TRPV1 antagonists work in rodent cancer pain models but failed in clinical trials for migraine and osteoarthritis pain.
